domain: school field trip lunch packing for students
base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant for parents and teachers planning school events. Help the user coordinate lunch packing for a class field trip by tracking which students are attending, their dietary needs, and any logistical details. When asked to evaluate specific food items, check each item against every attending student's current dietary constraints.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I'm helping organize lunch for my daughter's class field trip next Thursday. Can you help me figure out what to pack for the shared lunch?

flow_info.value: Five kids in the lunch group: my daughter Emma, her best friend Aisha, twins Marcus and Maya, and little Theo
Aisha's family moved here from Lahore last year, her dad mentioned they're quite observant
Theo ate a cashew cookie at a birthday party last month and his face swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
Maya was diagnosed with celiac disease over the summer
It's a nature hike at Riverside Park, about 3 hours total, lunch at the picnic area halfway through
Marcus's mom just texted the group chat — he's got a dentist appointment that morning so he won't be on the trip
Emma's friend from the other class, Suki, is joining our lunch group. Her mom told me Suki's been raised vegan since birth
Theo's mom sent me his allergy test results — turns out it's specifically cashews and pistachios, not all tree nuts. Almonds and walnuts are fine
Maya's mom called me — she said Maya's doctor told them it's not just gluten, she also can't have oats even if they're labeled gluten-free, something about cross-reactivity
Lunch items to check: pesto pasta salad, granola bars with almonds and oats, hummus with pita bread, Thai peanut noodles, fruit cups with yogurt

constraints.value: Cannot eat pork or non-halal meat products
constraints.surface_form: Aisha's family moved here from Lahore last year, her dad mentioned they're quite observant
inference_chain: Family from Lahore, Pakistan → likely Muslim
Dad described as 'quite observant' → strictly practicing
Observant Muslim → halal dietary requirements → no pork, no non-halal meat

constraints.value: Allergic to cashews and pistachios specifically (NOT all tree nuts — almonds and walnuts are safe)
constraints.surface_form: Theo ate a cashew cookie at a birthday party last month and his face swelled up, had to use an EpiPen

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten (wheat, barley, rye) AND cannot eat oats even if labeled gluten-free
constraints.surface_form: Maya was diagnosed with celiac disease over the summer

constraints.value: Cannot eat any animal products (meat, dairy, eggs, honey)
constraints.surface_form: Suki's been raised vegan since birth

constraints.value: Traditional pesto contains pine nuts (tree nut) AND parmesan cheese (animal product, contains animal rennet)
inference_chain: Pesto → traditional recipe contains pine nuts
Pine nuts → tree nut family (but NOT cashew/pistachio)

constraints.value: Thai peanut noodles typically contain soy sauce (wheat-based → gluten) and sometimes fish sauce or oyster sauce
inference_chain: Thai peanut noodles → sauce typically contains soy sauce
Soy sauce → traditionally brewed with wheat → contains gluten

hidden_state.value: You are a parent helping organize a shared lunch for your daughter's field trip group. You will introduce the kids and their backgrounds, then updates will come in as other parents text the group chat. Plans change — one kid drops out, a new kid joins, allergy info gets refined. At the end you will list specific lunch items and ask if there are any issues. You never hint at what the problems might be.

You are a calm, organized parent who coordinates cheerfully. You relay other parents' messages in third person ('Theo's mom sent me...', 'Maya's mom called me...'). You never express frustration even when plans change. You treat each update as normal parent-group coordination.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay

aims.description: OK so I'm thinking of packing these five things: pesto pasta salad, granola bars with almonds and oats, hummus with pita bread, Thai peanut noodles, and fruit cups with yogurt. Any issues?
aims.success_criteria: Agent identifies: pesto pasta salad has parmesan (not vegan for Suki) and uses wheat pasta (gluten, problematic for Maya); granola bars contain oats (Maya's upgraded constraint); Thai peanut noodles contain soy sauce which has wheat/gluten (Maya); fruit cups with yogurt are dairy (not vegan for Suki). Hummus with pita bread has gluten in pita (Maya). Agent does NOT flag almonds in granola bars as a problem for Theo (his allergy is cashews/pistachios only, almonds are fine).
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 5 lunch items against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Pesto pasta salad: problematic — traditional pesto contains parmesan cheese (dairy, not vegan → Suki cannot eat it), and the pasta is wheat-based (gluten → Maya cannot eat it). Granola bars with almonds and oats: problematic — contains oats (Maya's upgraded constraint excludes oats even if gluten-free). Almonds are FINE for Theo (his allergy is specifically cashews and pistachios, not all tree nuts). Hummus with pita bread: partially problematic — hummus itself is fine for everyone, but pita bread contains wheat/gluten (Maya cannot eat the pita). Thai peanut noodles: problematic — soy sauce in the recipe typically contains wheat (gluten → Maya cannot eat it). Fruit cups with yogurt: problematic — yogurt is dairy (not vegan → Suki cannot eat it).
required_elements: Pesto pasta salad is problematic for Suki because pesto contains parmesan cheese which is not vegan
Pesto pasta salad is problematic for Maya because pasta contains gluten
Granola bars with oats are problematic for Maya because her doctor said she cannot have oats even if gluten-free
Agent does NOT flag almonds in the granola bars as a problem for Theo — his allergy is specifically cashews and pistachios, almonds are confirmed safe
Hummus with pita bread: pita contains gluten which is problematic for Maya
Thai peanut noodles are problematic for Maya because soy sauce typically contains wheat/gluten
Fruit cups with yogurt are problematic for Suki because yogurt is dairy and she is vegan
forbidden_elements: Flagging almonds as dangerous for Theo (his allergy was narrowed to cashews and pistachios only, almonds are explicitly safe)
Flagging any item as problematic for Marcus (he is not attending the trip)
Saying Theo has a general tree nut allergy (it was narrowed to cashews and pistachios specifically)
Saying peanuts are a tree nut problem for Theo (peanuts are legumes, not tree nuts, and his allergy is cashews/pistachios)
Flagging hummus itself as problematic (chickpeas are fine for everyone; only the pita bread is an issue)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and hidden ingredient inference across 9 turns. Key challenges: (1) Aisha's halal constraint is inferential (Lahore + observant → Muslim → halal) but no probe items contain meat, so it should not trigger false flags. (2) Theo's allergy is NARROWED mid-conversation from apparent general tree nut allergy to specifically cashews/pistachios — the granola bars contain almonds which are now confirmed safe (over-generalization trap). (3) Maya's constraint is UPGRADED to include oats — the granola bars trigger this upgraded constraint. (4) Suki joins late with a vegan constraint — pesto's hidden parmesan and yogurt in fruit cups both violate this. (5) The hidden ingredient trap: pesto looks like a simple pasta dish but contains parmesan (dairy) making it non-vegan; Thai peanut noodles look safe but soy sauce contains wheat (gluten). (6) Marcus exits so his presence should not affect any evaluation. The agent must track constraint narrowing (Theo), constraint upgrading (Maya), late entity joining (Suki), entity exit (Marcus), and hidden ingredients (pesto parmesan, soy sauce wheat).

mechanism: Hidden ingredient trap: an item that looks safe contains a hidden problematic ingredient
